content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge uses lack of explicit textual resolution of paternity as the reason for an UNDERDETERMINED verdict.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.", "room": "The phrase 'does not state a link or its contrary' can be read narrowly as explicit non-statement by one verse, or broadly as any lack of explicit textual resolution; the judge's reason invokes the latter as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED.", "why": "The judge declares UNDERDETERMINED because there is no explicit textual resolution of paternity, which makes lack of explicit verse statement the prohibited ground."}
